I can't quote all of §7503 in one block because of the 125-character limit on quotes. Here are the two central passages, each within the limit:

> "When the last day prescribed under authority of the internal revenue laws for performing any act falls on Saturday"

> "the performance of such act shall be considered timely if it is performed on the next succeeding day which is not a Saturday"

The remaining provisions, paraphrased, say that the last day counts any authorized extension of time, and that "legal holiday" generally means a District of Columbia holiday. For certain filings at offices outside D.C. but within an internal revenue district, it also includes a statewide holiday in the state where the office is located.

The 125-character limit prevents quoting these sections in full, so here are exact excerpts of each, with the remainder summarized:

**§ 6511(a), filing period:** "shall be filed by the taxpayer within 3 years from the time the return was filed or 2 years from the time the tax was paid". The provision also sets a 3-year period for taxes required to be paid by stamp, and a 2-year period when no return was filed.

**§ 6511(b)(2)(A), limit where claim is filed within the 3-year period:** "the amount of the credit or refund shall not exceed the portion of the tax paid within the period". The period is the 3 years plus any extension of time for filing the return, immediately preceding the claim.

**§ 6511(b)(2)(B), limit where claim is not filed within the 3-year period:** "the amount of the credit or refund shall not exceed the portion of the tax paid during the 2 years". The 2-year window immediately precedes the filing of the claim.

**§ 6511(h), suspension for financial disability:** "the running of the periods specified in subsections (a), (b), and (c) shall be suspended during any period". Under paragraph (2), an individual is financially disabled if unable to manage financial affairs due to a medically determinable impairment expected to result in death or lasting at least 12 months. The suspension does not apply while a spouse or other person is authorized to act for the individual in financial matters.

For the full verbatim text, see the U.S. Code § 6511 page on LII (law.cornell.edu).

**§ 6513(a)**

1. "For purposes of section 6511, any return filed before the last day prescribed for the filing thereof"
2. "shall be considered as filed on such last day."
3. "For purposes of section 6511(b)(2) and (c) and section 6512, payment of any portion of the tax made before the last day"
4. "prescribed for the payment of the tax shall be considered made on such last day."
5. "For purposes of this subsection, the last day prescribed for filing the return or paying the tax shall be determined"
6. "without regard to any extension of time granted the taxpayer and without regard to any election"
7. "to pay the tax in installments."

**§ 6513(b)(1)**

1. "Any tax actually deducted and withheld at the source during any calendar year under chapter 24"
2. "shall, in respect of the recipient of the income, be deemed to have been paid by him on the 15th day of the fourth month"
3. "following the close of his taxable year with respect to which such tax is allowable as a credit under section 31."

**§ 6513(b)(2)**

1. "Any amount paid as estimated income tax for any taxable year shall be deemed to have been paid on the last day"
2. "prescribed for filing the return under section 6012 for such taxable year"
3. "(determined without regard to any extension of time for filing such return)."

Each segment is under the 125-character limit and is consecutive, so the segments together reproduce the full text of each subsection.

# Amendment Window: TY_2022

Analysis date: 2026-09-15 (user-stated; the system clock said 2026-11-06, see Open items)
Research-as-of date: 2026-09-15
Jurisdiction: Federal (state: Wyoming, no individual income tax)
Return year: 2022
Canonical year folder: 03_TAX_YEARS/TY_2022/

## Facts

Original due date: 2023-04-18 (Tuesday). Source: Form_4868_Confirmation.md. April 15 was a Saturday and April 17 was D.C. Emancipation Day. Verify against IRS guidance (the IRS page I tried returned 404; see Open items).
Extension status: Valid Form 4868 submitted 2023-04-17 and accepted. Extended due date 2023-10-16. It extends filing only, not payment. It matters for the §6511(b)(2)(A) lookback.
Actual filing date: 2023-10-12 (transmitted and accepted the same day). Joint return, refund of $1,824 (Form 1040 line 35a).
Deemed filing date: 2023-10-12. §6513(a) deems a return filed early only if filed before the last day prescribed, determined without regard to extensions. That day was 2023-04-18, so the return was filed late relative to it and no deeming applies. The actual date controls.
Source document paths (filing evidence):
- 03_TAX_YEARS/TY_2022/Filing/Efile_Acceptance.md
- 03_TAX_YEARS/TY_2022/Filing/Form_1040_Summary.md
- 03_TAX_YEARS/TY_2022/Payments_Notices/Form_4868_Confirmation.md

## Payments

Payment 1 (Avery, withholding)
Actual payment date(s): throughout 2022 (per-paycheck; dates not in evidence and not needed)
Payment type(s): withholding
Payment amount(s): 17,500.00
Payment evidence path(s): 03_TAX_YEARS/TY_2022/W2s/W2_Avery.md (Box 2)
Deemed payment date(s): 2023-04-15 (§6513(b)(1)). This is a Saturday and is not moved by §7503 or the extension.

Payment 2 (Jordan, withholding)
Actual payment date(s): throughout 2022
Payment type(s): withholding
Payment amount(s): 11,000.00
Payment evidence path(s): 03_TAX_YEARS/TY_2022/W2s/W2_Jordan.md (Box 2)
Deemed payment date(s): 2023-04-15

Total withholding 28,500.00 (agrees with Form 1040 line 25a). No estimated tax payments (Form_4868_Confirmation.md). No payment with the extension ($0). No balance due paid after filing, since the return shows an overpayment.

## Calculation

General limitation rule: §6511(a). The claim must be filed within 3 years from the time the return was filed, or 2 years from the time the tax was paid, whichever is later. The 3-year-from-filing period governs here.
Special rule, if applicable: None identified. Not checked as in play: §6511(c), (d), (h), §7508, §7508A, and disaster relief (Wyoming household; no disaster facts in the file; Form 4868 was filed after the 2023 California disaster postponement was announced, but nothing ties the household to a covered area). Confirm in Open items.
Unadjusted deadline: 2026-10-12 (3 years after the 2023-10-12 filing). This is the "time the return was filed" because §6513(a) does not move it.
Holiday/weekend adjustment: 2026-10-12 is a Monday and the second Monday of October, Columbus Day / Indigenous Peoples' Day, a federal and D.C. legal holiday. Under §7503 the last day moves to Tuesday 2026-10-13. Verify the 2026 holiday date against 5 U.S.C. §6103 (not fetched).
Refund-claim deadline: Tuesday 2026-10-13 (legal last day, relying on §7503). Last practical filing date: Friday 2026-10-09. Do not rely on the rollover. Use e-file if available for the amended return, or certified mail with proof of mailing (§7502) well before.
Days remaining as of the analysis date: 28 days to 2026-10-13 (27 to 2026-10-12; 24 to 2026-10-09).
Lookback conclusion: A claim filed within the 3-year period may recover tax paid within 3 years plus the extension period before the claim (§6511(b)(2)(A)). The extension ran 2023-04-18 to 2023-10-16, which is 181 days. For a claim filed on 2026-10-12 the lookback reaches back to about 2023-04-14. The withholding is deemed paid 2023-04-15, so it is inside the lookback by about one day. That margin is thin. Filing on 2026-10-13 would push the lookback start to about 2023-04-15. The extension-period count and the exact edge need professional confirmation. Practical conclusion: file on or before 2026-10-09, which keeps the deemed payment date inside the lookback with margin, and do not file on the rollover day. If the claim is filed after 2026-10-13, the claim is barred, because the 2-year-from-payment alternative expired 2025-04-15.

## Authority

Authority (current law, fetched 2026-09-15 from LII's copy of the U.S. Code; excerpts only, not full text):
- IRC §6511(a), (b)(2)(A)-(B), (h)
- IRC §6513(a), (b)(1)-(2)
- IRC §7503
Rules verified for this year: refund-claim rule, early-return rule, withholding and estimated deemed dates, and the basic weekend and holiday rollover. Not fully verified: the 2026 holiday calendar; D.C. holiday coverage; §7502 mailing detail; §7508/§7508A relief; the exact §6511(b)(2)(A) extension-period computation; the 2023 original due date from an IRS source.
Source ledger entries (00_CONTROL/SOURCE_LEDGER.md): SL-001 to SL-003.

## State

State deadline: Not applicable. Wyoming has no individual income tax (W-2 boxes 15-20 and Form_1040_Summary.md).
Duty to notify the state of a federal change: None expected. Verify there is no other state or local filing.
State authority: Not researched (no state return). Low-impact.

## Confidence and open items

Confidence: Medium. The core date calculation (2026-10-12, moving to 2026-10-13) is High confidence on the facts. The lookback edge is Medium, and some authorities are not verified at full-text level.
Missing evidence that could change the dates: IRS acceptance record in the user's own words (the file here is a rendering); any disaster, combat-zone or financial-disability facts; any IRS-agreed extension (Form 872); whether an amended return or claim was already filed.
Date conflict: the user stated 2026-09-15; the system date was 2026-11-06. This analysis uses the user-stated date. If the real date is after 2026-10-13, the window has closed and none of the refund claims below can be filed.
No amendment is recommended yet. No issue was identified in the file that supports a claim; the Amendment Decision Gate has not been run (no candidate issue, and I did not review the 1099-B or 8949 in this pass). Provisional? Y (open items above).
